correctness.rationale: Stable suffix 1101 and no-00 boundaries force a unique crossing site for first (01)^k. Explicit finite base and induction give all positions; orientation shift and end extension classify all alternating words; the longest-factor law follows from the first-containing stages. Checker independently compares the first 19 literal iterates; no finite experiment is substituted for the induction.

evidence: Shallit Theorem 7 proves existence of all binary factors avoiding 00; Theorem 4 gives first positions for 1^n, not the first appearances of (01)^k.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Factor language and extremal first-position bounds are strictly weaker data than the exact positional spectrum. The prior extremal statement leaves many lower-ranked pattern positions undetermined and gives no stagewise maximum alternation formula.
